Environment management · Lesson 0002

Who loads .env?

Bun and npm look similar at the command line, but they do not make the same promise.

Target time: 7 minutes · Builds on the process boundary

A file cannot export itself

Suppose your project contains:

# .env
API_URL=https://api.example

That file changes nothing until a loader reads it. A loader parses the file and puts values into a process environment. Your shell, runtime, framework, or deployment tool may be the loader—but you must identify which one.

Debugging rule: do not ask “Does this project support .env?” Ask “Which exact process loads this file, and what child processes inherit the result?”

Bun loads; npm launches

CommandWho handles `.env`?
bun app.tsBun automatically loads its supported dotenv files.
bun run startBun loads dotenv, then starts the package script with those values.
npm run startnpm provides a script environment, but does not document automatic dotenv loading.
node --env-file=.env app.jsNode explicitly loads the named file.

The Bun documentation explicitly promises automatic loading. The npm scripts documentation lists the environment npm creates but makes no automatic dotenv promise. Modern Node offers an explicit --env-file mechanism.

Do not overgeneralize: npm run dev may still appear to load .env when the script starts Vite, Next.js, Bun, or another tool that performs the loading. npm is then the launcher, not the loader.

Follow the process chain

Given this package script:

{
  "scripts": {
    "start:node": "node app.js",
    "start:bun": "bun app.ts"
  }
}

npm run start:node creates this chain:

npm
does not load `.env`
→
Node
no explicit loader

npm run start:bun creates a different ending:

npm
does not load `.env`
→
Bun
loads `.env`

Once Bun loads the value, code inside Bun reads it through process.env.API_URL, Bun.env.API_URL, or import.meta.env.API_URL. Bun documents these as aliases.

Turn Bun's loader off deliberately

bun run --no-env-file app.ts

Use --no-env-file in CI/CD or production when the platform is the authority and you want Bun to rely only on the process environment. Bun also supports an explicit file:

bun --env-file=.env.staging app.ts

These flags are defined in Bun's environment-variable documentation.

Retrieval check

Assume plain commands with no framework. Each answer has two words and thirteen characters.

A project has API_URL=example in .env, then runs bun app.ts.

The same project runs npm run start:node from the script above.

The same project runs npm run start:bun from the script above.

The project runs bun run --no-env-file app.ts.
